note: Stand-in content for stages 3 to 6 until audit.json, dialogue.json and explain.json have schemas. Converted from prototype/data/sample-horde.js.

dialogue.question: roam.cpp registers a function pointer that processor.cpp later calls into kuramoto_core. I drew that as an inferred edge from ROAM to kuramoto_core. Should ROAM sit in Dynamics, or is it a SAW feature?
dialogue.answer: Dynamics. ROAM is a coupling law, same family as consonance gravity.
dialogue.effect: Kept ROAM in Dynamics. The edge stays inferred until a runtime trace confirms it.

dialogue.question: state_io.cpp and quantum_morph.cpp both serialize corner presets. Should I group them as a Presets cluster, or keep quantum_morph under Modulation?
Nothing in the repo calls lfsr_noise::reseed(). Is it dead code, or does the host thread call it by name?
multistage_shaper.cpp uses the ADAA helper from FOUNDATIONS, but WARP's simplex_shaper.cpp does not. Is that intentional, given the 2× oversampling ceiling?
dialogue.answer: Not intentional. WARP predates the ADAA helper.
dialogue.effect: Sent to the audit swarm and added to the WARP explainer.

audit.text: Audio bus contract holds. All five engine outputs call render(AudioBlock&) with stereo float32.
Dynamics has 1 internal edge and 4 edges into kuramoto_core. It behaves like part of SAW. Suggest nesting it under SAW or renaming it Coupling laws.
audit.reply: Keep it top-level. CHOIR will couple through it once vowel coupling lands.

audit.text: ROAM → kuramoto_core is inferred. A runtime trace shows it fires only when ROAM is enabled. Mark the edge conditional.
No cycles between FOUNDATIONS and the engines. Every FOUNDATIONS edge points inward.
parity_tests.cpp compares against goldens generated by the browser prototypes, which live outside this repo. That dependency is missing from the graph.
simplex_shaper → fx_router is counted toward the Audio bus but is only inferred through an engine table. Confirm it statically before counting it toward the contract.

flow: The host calls clap_entry, which hands each audio block to processor.
processor runs the mod matrix and resolves the morph before any sound is made.
voice_alloc hands note events to engine voices.
Engines render into the Audio bus, which feeds fx_router.
fx_router runs filter, phaser, time and shaper stages in order.
Every stage reads its settings through the Param bus.

notes.file:src/engines/saw/kuramoto_core.cpp: Integrates the coupled phases for each voice. K runs from −1 (splay) to +1 (lock).
notes.file:src/mod/quantum_morph.cpp: Resolves each parameter to one of four corner presets by a weighted coin flip.
notes.file:src/mod/intent_bus.cpp: Macros and the XY pad write intents. Each corner binds intents to parameters with a depth and range.
notes.file:src/mod/inertia.cpp: Mass-spring smoothing applied to detune, glide and modulation.
notes.file:src/dynamics/roam.cpp: Chord tones as potential wells in log-frequency space, with thermal wander.
notes.file:src/dynamics/consonance_gravity.cpp: Pulls chord intervals toward just intonation.
notes.file:src/engines/warp/simplex_shaper.cpp: Blends 7 transfer curves; the weights always sum to one.
notes.file:verify: Bit-level parity against the browser prototypes.
notes.file:foundations/param_store.hpp: Single source of parameter values. Every read is smoothed per block.
notes.file:src/fx/fx_router.cpp: Receives the Audio bus and routes it through the FX chain.
notes.file:src/plugin/processor.cpp: The audio callback. Hands each block to the voices, then to the FX chain.
notes.file:foundations/voice_alloc.cpp: Assigns incoming notes to engine voices.
notes.art:tests/goldens/*.bin: Reference renders produced by the browser prototypes.

steps.text: The host delivers a note event with the audio block.
The audio callback forwards events before rendering.
Picks a free SAW voice, or steals the oldest.
Starts the voice and sets its pitch target.
Couples the voice's oscillators; the phases settle according to K.
The voice output arrives on the Audio bus.
Last stage in the default chain before output.

tours.title: Where does the XY pad write?

steps.text: Dragging the pad writes an intent, not a parameter.
Intent values fan out to each corner's bindings.
Each block, every parameter resolves to a corner.
Changes go through a mass-spring so they glide.
Final smoothing before the DSP reads the value.
Renders each engine offline and diffs against the goldens.
Reference output from the browser prototypes. Parity with them is not the same as sounding right.
One of four engines under test.
